stories.title: Holy shit holy shit holy shit holy shit: The magnitude of what's now happening
stories.blurb: Scott Aaronson — quantum complexity theorist and longtime AI skeptic — is apparently losing his mind over something happening in AI right now, and the HN comment section is on fire with 1734 responses. When the guy who spent years pumping the brakes writes a post titled like this, you read it immediately. Essential context for anyone building with AI tools in late 2026.

stories.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
stories.blurb: The NYT is telling its photographers to freeze their Photoshop installs to avoid Adobe's latest AI-generated content features — a major institutional pushback against AI contaminating photojournalism workflows. This is the first major newsroom to draw a hard line, and it won't be the last. Creative professionals should pay attention to where "helpful" AI features end and editorial integrity begins.

stories.title: Much shorter version of GRH Lean verification from Anthropic
stories.blurb: A community member has produced a dramatically condensed version of Anthropic's Lean formal verification of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis result, making the proof more auditable and accessible. This is a landmark moment for AI-assisted mathematics — formal verification at this level was science fiction a few years ago. Directly relevant if you've been following Anthropic's AI-driven math research.

stories.title: GPT-6.2 Astra is the first model to beat Googlers' code golf records
stories.blurb: GPT-6.2 Astra just topped a code golf leaderboard that veteran Googlers have held for years — a concrete, measurable benchmark showing AI surpassing expert humans at code optimization. The interactive leaderboard lets you drill into the solutions yourself. If you're using AI coding assistants, this is a useful data point on where the ceiling actually is now.

stories.title: OpenAI cuts GPT-6.2 usage: Astra hits limits 40% faster, Sol 25% faster
stories.blurb: Just as GPT-6.2 Astra is breaking records, OpenAI is quietly throttling usage limits — Astra burning through quotas 40% faster than before. This is the capacity crunch that follows every major model launch, and it's particularly painful for developers who've built workflows around these models. Plan your rate limit budgets accordingly.

stories.title: Nfs2root: A 12-year-old pre-auth remote root in the Linux kernel's NFS server
stories.blurb: A pre-authentication remote root exploit hiding in the Linux kernel's NFS server for over a decade — no credentials needed to own the box. If you run any Linux servers with NFS exposed, patch now and check your exposure. The write-up is detailed and worth reading to understand the vulnerability class.

stories.title: Slow Ubuntu security response times
stories.blurb: A detailed oss-security post documents Canonical taking unacceptably long to patch reported vulnerabilities in Ubuntu — sometimes months after upstream fixes are available. For teams running Ubuntu in production, this is a sobering audit of the security SLA you're actually getting. The 230-comment HN thread has strong opinions from both defenders and critics.

stories.title: Intel One Mono font
stories.blurb: Intel's expressive monospace font is making the rounds again on HN with 360 upvotes and a lively thread debating it against Monaspace, Cascadia Code, and JetBrains Mono. It's open source, designed for legibility at small sizes, and has great ligature support. Worth a 10-minute trial in your editor.

stories.title: Minipg: PostgreSQL as a Single Executable
stories.blurb: Minipg bundles PostgreSQL into a single self-contained binary — no install, no system dependencies, just run it. This is a game-changer for local dev environments, CI pipelines, and embedded scenarios where you want real Postgres semantics without the setup overhead. Try it today in your .NET or Angular dev workflow.

stories.title: Collection of preserved UI style guides
stories.blurb: A beautifully curated archive of historical UI style guides from companies like Apple, Microsoft, Atari, and NeXT — the actual design bibles that shaped our screens. Invaluable for anyone interested in the history of interface design or looking for inspiration for design system documentation. The Apple Human Interface Guidelines entries alone are worth the visit.

stories.title: https://www.macstories.net/stories/a-closer-look-at-claudes-mac-apps/
stories.blurb: MacStories takes a deep dive into Anthropic's Claude Mac apps — the same AI you use in Claude Code, now with a polished native macOS experience. If you're already a Claude Code user, understanding how the desktop apps work and what they expose is immediately actionable. This is the definitive early look at Claude on the platform.

stories.title: Anatomy of Apple's Personal Knowledge Graph — Eighth Rank
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: security, mac, apple
stories.blurb: An interactive breakdown of how Apple Intelligence builds and queries a personal knowledge graph from your on-device data — contacts, calendars, messages, documents. For anyone who cares about privacy and the Apple ecosystem, understanding exactly what data Apple Intelligence is indexing and how it's isolated is crucial. Well-structured and surprisingly accessible.

stories.title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now | The Verge
stories.blurb: Anthropic has shipped autonomous PR review and self-fixing capabilities for Claude — it can now read a pull request, spot issues, write a fix, and open a new PR without human intervention. For Claude Code users this is a significant workflow upgrade. Expect this to reshape how small teams handle code review overhead.

stories.title: Anthropic, OpenAI employees fear models are too unsafe to release
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: AI, future, check, danger
stories.blurb: Axios reports that employees at both Anthropic and OpenAI are raising internal alarms about models currently in development being too dangerous to release publicly. This is a rare moment of public whistleblowing from inside the labs, and it comes as model capabilities are accelerating sharply. Essential reading for anyone thinking seriously about AI risk.

stories.title: "if you can imagine and then clearly describe a piece of software, Fable can build it"
stories.blurb: Simon Willison's latest on LLM inflection points includes a striking claim about Fable — that natural language software descriptions are now sufficient to build working apps end-to-end. Willison is careful and credible, so when he's this excited, it's worth paying attention. Directly relevant if you're evaluating AI coding tools beyond Claude Code.

stories.title: 1Password breach leaked customer names and emails, but not passwords | The Verge
stories.blurb: 1Password confirmed a data breach exposing customer names and email addresses — the vault contents are reportedly safe, but the exposure of account identifiers opens the door to targeted phishing. If you use 1Password (and many Apple-ecosystem devs do), be on alert for convincing follow-on attacks. Enable phishing-resistant MFA if you haven't already.

stories.title: AI is moving way too fast
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: to_share, forecasting, productivity, anthropic, coding-tools, statistical-modeling, future-analysis
stories.blurb: Nate Silver — forecasting heavyweight — examines the "uncanny" pace of AI in 2026, where coding tools are delivering miraculous productivity gains while social and political institutions lag dangerously behind. He brings actual statistical rigor to the question of AI trajectory, which makes this more grounded than most hot takes. Good long-read for a holiday.

stories.title: Predicting LoRA size for any dataset
stories.blurb: A practical guide to estimating how large a LoRA adapter needs to be before you spend hours training it — covers dataset size, rank selection, and expected parameter counts. If you're fine-tuning local models with Unsloth or similar tools, this saves real time and GPU cost. Bookmark-worthy reference.

stories.title: FireCrawl
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: api, markdown, website
stories.blurb: FireCrawl turns any website into clean, LLM-ready Markdown via a simple API — handles JS-rendered pages, pagination, and auth. If you're building RAG pipelines, feeding context to Claude Code, or scraping docs for your Obsidian vault, this is a drop-in solution that actually works. Free tier available.

stories.title: GitHub - ersinkoc/phonebox: Turn an old Android phone into a customizable desk panel and touch control deck
stories.blurb: PhoneBox repurposes an old Android phone as a 124-widget touch control deck for macOS — think Stream Deck but free, and running on hardware you already own. It includes widgets for system stats, AI coding shortcuts, media control, and automation triggers, with 30 ready-made templates. Genuinely actionable for a macOS developer looking to extend their desk setup.
